Inference: HUD's existing proration method for mixed families (24 CFR 5.520) implements Section 214 of the Housing and Community Development Act of 1980, so a final rule that ends proration may draw statutory challenges.

proposal: The Mandate recommends that HUD restart the 2019 proposed rule that would prohibit noncitizens, including all mixed-status families, from living in federally assisted housing, and align with DHS public-charge reforms. It states that local welfare organizations, not the federal government, should house noncitizens.
remaining: HUD must review comments, publish a final rule, and set an effective date.
Existing mixed-status households would then have 90 days after the effective date to submit proof of eligible status under the proposal.
The proposal keeps a limited deferral for some long-assisted families, which is narrower than a complete bar.

review.mandate_note: Page 509 asks HUD to restart the 2019 Trump proposed rule barring noncitizens, including all mixed-status families, from federally assisted housing and to align with DHS public charge reforms; footnote 33 on page 515 cites the 2019-05-10 proposed rule.

source_checks.note: Confirms the proposed rule at 91 FR 8151 with comments due 2026-04-21: verification for every member regardless of age (removing the age-62 exemption), proration only while verification is pending, removal of the do-not-contend option, and a 90-day compliance window for mixed families after the effective date. It retains statutory preservation assistance for families assisted on 1995-06-19 (HUD's administrative date in place of the statutory 1988-02-05), not a 1988 date as the summary says, and it does not bar mixed-status families outright.

significance.rationale: Barring mixed-status families from assisted housing would remove eligibility for roughly 25,000 households.

status_summary: HUD published a new proposed rule on 2026-02-20 (91 FR 8151) that would require immigration or citizenship verification for every household member regardless of age, limit proration of assistance for mixed-status families to the period while verification is pending, and remove the option to decline to claim eligible status. Statutory preservation assistance would remain for families assisted as of HUD's 1995-06-19 reference date, so the proposal does not bar every mixed-status family outright. Comments closed 2026-04-21 and no final rule appeared in HUD's Federal Register listings through 2026-10-05. Separately, a 2025-11-26 HUD notice states that HUD reads PRWORA's federal-public-benefit definition to cover several HUD grant programs and says verification guidance will follow.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14218 (Ending Taxpayer Subsidization of Open Borders) is signed; HUD's 2026 proposal cites it as a basis.
HUD publishes a notice interpreting 'federal public benefit' under PRWORA to cover a range of HUD grant and housing programs, with immigration-verification guidance to follow.
HUD posts a pre-publication copy of the proposed rule 'Housing and Community Development Act of 1980: Verification of Eligible Status'.
Proposed rule published at 91 FR 8151: universal status verification, temporary-only proration, end of the 'do not contend' option; 60-day comment period.
Comment period closes. Housing and immigrant-advocacy groups filed opposing comments; no final rule or lawsuit found afterward.

title: Bar noncitizens, including mixed-status families, from federally assisted housing
uncertainties: Estimates of affected households (about 80,000 people per an advocacy group's 2025 analysis) are from advocacy sources, not HUD; HUD's own docket estimates are in the Federal Register text. I could not run a general web search for 2026 lawsuits, OMB review of a final rule, or congressional action on the same topic, and did not verify what the 2025 reconciliation law did on this subject. Whether a final rule that ends proration fits Section 214 is a legal question I did not resolve (my inference from the statute described in HUD's own proposal).
